about: PROPOSED, UNSIGNED. One new Proofline task, XC-126: balance the vv shards by each task's measured seconds instead of its position in the contract, because the position split put XC-26 (7.3 minutes) and XC-02 in one shard, which reached 15.6 minutes against XC-125's 15 and a job limit of 20. Nothing here is binding and CI does not read this file; it becomes part of the contract only when the owner key signs it into proofline.json.

tasks.title: vv shards are balanced by measured task cost instead of contract position
tasks.description: XC-125 split vv into six shards by contract position (task k runs in shard k mod 6), and the shard receipts already record each task's seconds. Measured on 27 Oct 2026 from the six shard receipts of each of CI runs 40524709931, 40527561807 and 40530600132: the 109 tasks take 47.3 minutes in total (median per task), and XC-26 alone takes 439 seconds, 7.3 minutes. Position puts XC-26 and XC-02 (86 s) in shard 2, so shard 2 summed 11.4, 12.5 and 15.0 minutes while shard 1 summed 5.5, 4.0 and 4.5. On run 40530600132 the shard 2 job took 15.6 minutes, over the 15 that XC-125-AC06 states, against a job limit of 20; on that run every task in shard 2 slowed by about the same factor (the 20-second tasks took 29), so runner speed moves the total and the position split leaves no room for it. Simulated on the median costs, position mod 6 gives a largest shard of 12.5 minutes and position mod 8 gives 13.6; a cost-based split gives 7.9 on six shards, which is the ideal of 47.3/6, and 7.3 on eight, where XC-26 alone is the floor. So the fix is the split, not more shards, and no timeout changes. tools/vv.py costs DIR reads the shard (or merged) receipts under DIR and writes vv/costs.json: the median seconds per task over those receipts, rounded to 0.1, the source run ids given with --run, sorted keys and no timestamp, so the same receipts give the same bytes. When vv/costs.json is present, --shard I/N assigns tasks longest first (by cost, then contract position) to the shard with the smallest running total (ties to the lowest index); a task with no cost entry counts as the median known cost; each shard runs its tasks in contract order. Without the file, the split is exactly XC-125's position rule. Each shard receipt records the split it used (cost or position) and the sha256 of vv/costs.json, and tools/vv.py merge recomputes every shard's tasks from the checkout's file and fails closed when the shards disagree on the split or the costs hash, when a shard's hash is not the checkout's file, or when a shard's tasks are not its cost partition. tools/vv.py costs --predict prints the largest shard's predicted minutes for the vv-shard matrix size in ci.yml. vv/costs.json joins the vv component in tools/interdeps.py so every tracked file stays covered. The cost file is refreshed by hand from a recent main run when the split drifts; it only changes which shard runs a task, and every task is still verified on every run.

criteria.statement: With a cost file, --shard I/N assigns every contract task to exactly one shard, deterministically, for N from 1 to 8; each shard lists its tasks in contract order; a task with no cost counts as the median cost; and the largest shard's total is at most the mean shard total plus the largest single task
Without vv/costs.json the split is exactly XC-125's position rule, task k in shard k mod N

tools/vv.py costs takes the median seconds per task over the receipts it reads, writes byte-identical output for the same receipts, names the source runs, and refuses a receipt that has no per-task seconds

The merge fails closed: shards that disagree on the split or on the costs hash, a shard whose costs hash is not the checkout's vv/costs.json, and a shard whose tasks are not its cost partition each exit 1 with ok false
Sharded by cost and merged, a contract gives the same per-task states and pass counts as one unsharded run on the same tree, for N of 2, 3 and 6, with one failing claimed task
The committed vv/costs.json has a cost for every task in proofline.json and names at least one source CI run

verifier.cmd: python3 -c "import json,sys;c=json.load(open('vv/costs.json'));t=[x['id'] for x in json.load(open('proofline.json'))['tasks']];m=[i for i in t if i not in c.get('seconds',{})];print(m);sys.exit(0 if not m and c.get('source_runs') else 1)"

criteria.statement: Predicted from vv/costs.json for the matrix size in ci.yml, the largest shard is 9 minutes or less
On the pull request's CI run, every vv-shard job finished in 12 minutes or less (run id and per-shard minutes from the jobs API in evidence/XC-126.json)

verifier.cmd: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('evidence/XC-126.json'));m=[s['minutes'] for s in d['shards']];print(json.dumps({'max_shard_minutes':max(m) if len(m)>=3 and d.get('run_id') else 999}))"

criteria.statement: docs/VV.md explains the cost-based split and how to refresh vv/costs.json
Every changed file is inside this task's scope

stop_rules: If a criterion cannot pass, STOP and report what blocks it, what was tried and what is needed. Never weaken a criterion, skip a test or raise a timeout to make it pass.
Every verifier runs as written on every run; the cost file only decides which shard runs a task, and no task is skipped, cached or dropped because of its cost.
The vv-shard matrix size and every timeout-minutes in ci.yml stay as they are; if 12 minutes per shard cannot be met by the split alone, STOP and report the measured shard minutes.
